items.note: S2.4.1 states the eight-row schedule of copy/gather/scatter/side-injection, y_S <- y_S + x_S for arbitrary scratch, the exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoration (lines 728-739), but says 'three such stages' where stage 2 is the inverse schedule from Y to X (731-732, 768-770), and omits h=100, the triple indexing and N, m. The net-change argument (J V + R G)x (749-766) is only alluded to in S2.4.3.1, so it is not derived.

Follows the paper's invariant argument (frames per vertex, edge change D_v D_u^{-1}, common frame commutes with pointwise gate, D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, intermediate frames free). The route operator drops the scalar sign epsilon_w (819-821), and S2.4.2 writes D_out D_in^{-1} without S_Omega.

Statement matches Lemma lem:motif-residuals (comparable labels, only central 3->4 edges decrease by h, L=Ich, sum = Wm-2N+2L) and the ratios 100/539, 101/539. The derivation gives the indicator inner products but skips the label construction (A, P, B, Q, stage transitions, gate-label table eq:motif-labels) and the telescoping of signed changes at gates (1066-1071).

States s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m and the endpoint identity I_m, and derives the rank sum faithfully (P_V-P_U rank, N source exceptions of rank one, deficit N-2L_b). It never defines the shear frames Phi_M or says the network therefore applies H <- H + D on every role (1124-1136), and the endpoint computation P_{U_a^perp} - (-P_{U_a}) = I_m (1169-1171) is not shown.

S2.4.3.5 correctly states the kernel-per-orthonormal-basis-vector factorization and s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c < W_c m, but omits the phase frames C_U and the conclusion that, after diagonal corrections, every role receives C^{tensor m} (1225-1228). The weight-additivity proof (1232-1260) is not reconstructed.

L/N < 1/2, s<Wm for both networks, deficits above 20*2^{-50}, log m < 20 and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} are stated, but the exact relative deficits eta_b, eta_c are missing. The inequality m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-20*2^{-50}) > m(1-eta) (1334-1336) is not shown, so this is stated rather than derived.

Elementary stream operations are stated correctly. For the controlled shift, S2.3 drops the b^{O(1)} offset-preparation condition from its claim and omits multiplication by fixed rational units (569-570). Its 'split each fiber at the offset and merge in the opposite order' matches 575-580.

Factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 and the three-step trick with one interchange per one of Pi follow the paper (1432-1443). The plan omits the fixed odd prime q avoiding all denominators and the specialization to Z/q^b (1396-1405, 1413-1423), which the shear needs to be valid. The elimination proof of the factorization (1375-1391) is not given.

Row split into W role streams of volume V/W, middle-shear-only network use, s recursive calls, the recurrence, the two-case geometric sum and the O(V) fixed-tape parking all follow 1491-1588. That the shear frames give H <- H + D on every row is only implicit via S2.4.3.4 and S2.4.2.

Matches the proof: top rho digits joined as a row field at cost O(V rho), padding rows to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces handled by the power-width procedure summing to O(V e^tau), and padding [2^u] to [q^e] with e=O(u).

Identities for C, conjugation into coordinate slots, s_c children on e/m axes, the inverse-child formula and H_0^{tensor D} = b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D are all correct. Missing: P_M as a fixed number of F_2 row additions (1892-1901), and the endpoint corrections giving C^{tensor e} on every role (1907-1913).

The eight operations, the bad set with |B| <= delta_bad M, and the sort-based repair follow the proof. The plan never says how a rotation is executed: by chunk swaps (Lemma chunk-swap, O(V L^tau)) that place the target after its controls, then a controlled shift (2117-2155). That is the source of the L^tau term. Nor does it say that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes only B (2107-2114).

Rows from the first q_0 chunks, the u=Wg+w split, the recurrence with leaves F(e)=O(e), the leaf bound and the base-m sum match. The step that turns the node overhead O((eK)^tau+1) into O(e^lambda) via K <= e^{c/beta} and tau(1+c/beta) < lambda (2413-2415) is missing; S2.6.3.3 cites only a < m^lambda.

Output Q_p(H z) in O(V d^{lambda'}) with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}, and exact evaluation with guard width ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) = o(p), are stated correctly. The guard-width derivation (depth recurrence A(e) <= s A(e/m) + E, 2479-2560) is asserted, not shown.

Character cancellation, decimation in frequency, bit-reversed storage and the grouped rounds H then J_E follow 2819-2914. The layout L (prefix-slot moves, at most Dq-1 width-K chunk exchanges, 2990-3032) and the error/cost bound appear only as an inferred statement in S3.2.

Evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, four products by the established multiplier, the separation bound |h_j| <= r 2^{2p} < 2^{3p} < B_0/2, carry-based centered extraction and reduction mod y^r+1 match the proof.

Route (two forward transforms in common LB order, pointwise signed-packed products, opposite transform, normalization F^-(f*g) = M F^-f F^-g) matches 3415-3441, and the retained-order commutation is in the motivation. The error chain 2 delta + eta, then 3 delta + eta, times M (3443-3473) is not derived.

Statements of the one-dimensional identity, approximation error/cost, tensor form with gamma = 2 d alpha^2, linewise cost and exposure cost match. The Gaussian construction of A, B_0 (3576-3792) is not reconstructed, so it is only stated.

Both the permuted chirp identity with the correct chirp and the source-permutation cancellation (u*v)/S^2 are stated correctly. Their proofs (3938-3988) are not shown, and conjugation for RF_s^+ is not mentioned.

Fixed exponents, sizes, the prime-interval count and the conclusions T/2 < S < T and alpha^4 theta_i > p are correct, but eta = 1/(4d) and alpha = ceil((12 d^2 b)^{1/4}) (4091) are never given. Those choices are what yield (1-1/(2d))^d > 1/2 and alpha^4 theta > 3db >= p (4138-4150).
Definition with mu_i = P_i^{-1} mod s_i, isomorphism by order S, triangular coordinates b_i, prefix-controlled cyclic shifts and O(d^2) axis moves by chunk swap match the paper.

The exact isometric isomorphism and wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h = zeta^j are reconstructed faithfully. The linewise interface M_C(f,g) = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) = (f*g)/T (4321-4342) and the computed version's error are absent.

Chirp transform, source transform with exact counterpart RF_s, the six steps and the two scales by S follow the paper. Digit scaling by 2^{-b-2} and the conjugation definition of the opposite transform are not mentioned (minor).

The final part of the chain (norm .26, E_w = S(3E_s+2), 448 b 2^{-b+gamma} <= 448 b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2, rounding, carries) matches. The earlier error chain leading to E_s = 9 2^gamma T L and the use of gamma <= b/4 are not shown.
All seven rows, their powers, the margin minimum g_2 = 2^{-181} = 2 kappa, and the final O(Tp p^{1-kappa}) bound match. The schoolbook cutoff for small n is omitted (minor).

S1 refers to the Schoenhage-Strassen n log n order and the page integer-multiplication-conjecture, but nowhere states the liminf negation argument that the bound refutes an eventual c_A n lg n lower bound.

errors.says: Since Harvey and van der Hoeven reached O(n log n), 'a further saving must beat a logarithmic factor by a power'.
errors.paper: The paper only reports that it obtains a strict power saving in the logarithmic factor; it does not claim that any further saving must be a power saving.

errors.says: A route from w to rho(w) applies D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}; S2.4.2 calls the endpoint operator D_out D_in^{-1}.
errors.paper: The implemented operator is D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and the route applies epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} with the scalar sign epsilon_w. That sign matters in the complex network, where the X outputs must be negated.

errors.says: Three such stages (forward invocations) exchange the banks.
errors.paper: Stage 1 and stage 3 are forward invocations from X to Y; stage 2 is the inverse schedule from Y to X, which effects X <- X - Y.

errors.says: The network has W wires of rank-m labels.
errors.paper: Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of the m-dimensional space F^{tensor 3}, of varying dimension from 0 (scratch sources) to m (sinks); only the ambient space has dimension m.

errors.says: A rational m x m shear (H,D) -> (H+AD,D) of rank a costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V).
errors.paper: The shear is over Z/q^b for a fixed odd prime q chosen to avoid all denominators and diagonal numerators of the fixed factorizations; only then do the rational identities specialize.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: the scalar exchange network, frames, labels with s<Wm, matrix shear and the interchange recurrence give O(V u^tau). The phase-frame network, packed row additions and the layer recurrence give O(V d^{lambda'}). These feed the synthetic transforms and convolution, Gaussian resampling with chirp and permutation cancellation, the CRT map and twist, exact recovery and the seven-row cost table with min margin 2kappa. It thins out wherever a lemma is only asserted: the label construction, the source of the L^tau term in packed additions, the overhead-to-e^lambda step, guard widths, the transform layout, Gaussian resampling and the early error chain. It does not break.

steps.note: The exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with restored scratch wires and the eight-row gate schedule are stated. h=100, the indexing of data pairs by triples in T^3, N = binom(h,3)^3 and m = h^3 never appear, so the defining quantities of the fixed network are missing.
Common frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, the array network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and edges pay only D_v D_u^{-1}. The route sign epsilon_w is dropped (minor).

Nondegenerate subspace labels in F^{tensor 3}, comparable labels on every edge, and only central 3->4 edges decreasing, each by h, are stated. The ambient dimension m appears only loosely, as 'rank-m labels' in S2.4.
P_V - P_U has rank dim V - dim U, and the N source edges are the exceptions, each of rank one (2P_{U_a}).
Sum of |Delta dim| = Wm - 2N + 2L with L = Ich, and s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b, are both stated.
L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539 are below 1/2, and the deficit N - 2L_b > 0, hence s_b < W_b m.

S2.4.3.4 states that the endpoint matrices differ by I_m on every input role, and S2.4.6.2 has the network perform the middle shear H <- H + D. The shear frames Phi_M are not named explicitly, so the link is somewhat implicit.
The rank-a shear factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V), so a node makes exactly s recursive calls. The prime q and the modular specialization are omitted.
Children of volume V/W, F_k <= (s/W) F_{k-1} + O(1), s/W < m^tau with tau = 1 - 2^{-50} from deficits above 20*2^{-50} and log m < 20, and F_k = O(e^tau) via the two-case geometric sum.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the central saving almost completely. Frames, labels, rank = dimension change with the N source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L, the strict deficit from L/N < 1/2, the endpoint identity, edges as rank-many recursive calls and the recurrence with tau = 1 - 2^{-50} are all present with their defining content. The one gap is the fixed network's parameters (h=100, triple indexing, N, m = h^3), which are never given, so C1 is only mentioned.
